newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL downgrades Flex Industries to "A".
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL downgrades Flex Industries to "A".

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) on Wednesday downgraded from "A+" to "A" the rating assigned to the Non-Convertible and Partly Convertible Debenture programmes of Flex Industries Limited (FIL).
The firm said in a statement that the new rating indicated adequate safety of timely payment of interest and principal.

The existing Fixed Deposit programme of the company has also been downgraded from "FAA-" to "FA+", CRISIL said. This rating indicates that the degree of safety regarding timely instrument on the instrument is adequate.
The revised ratings for FIL's debenture and fixed deposit programmes reflect CRISIL's concern that the company is unlikely to retain profit margins at the past levels, the statement said.
FIL has gradually expanded its laminating and converting capacities over the last 5-6 years, CRISIL said.

The expansion programme undertaken by the company in the last two years, at a cost of about 3.2 billion rupees, has increased the installed capacity of laminates to 25,000 MT, PET (Poly Ethylene Terephthalate) films to 24,000 MT and BOPP (Biaxially Oriened Poly Propylene) films to 15,000 MT.

Both the BOPP and PET film industries currently face a large over-capacity in the domestic market. This over-supply situation has affected the profitability of all Indian manufacturers, with the situation is likely to continue in the short to medium term.

As a result of these projects, FIL is presently the only backward integrated laminate manufacturer in the country. But the capacities set up by the company are significantly higher than those required for captive consumption.

"As a result, the business profile of FIL has undergone a substantial change from a low capital intensive, relatively less cyclical laminate business which provided enough scope for product differentiation to a high capital intensive, cyclical film business which is more of a commodity business," it added.
The revised ratings also reflect CRISIL's concern at FIL's capital structure and weak coverage ratios given high levels of high cost borrowings and pressures on profitability.
